decisive_items: Fungal skin culture: black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species
Infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation (Fontana-Masson)

Histopathology showed pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, foamy histiocytes, neutrophils, and multinucleate giant cells along with pigmented hyphae
response.rationale: The culture definitively identifies Exophiala spinifera, a causative agent of phaeohyphomycosis, and the histopathology shows pigmented yeasts and hyphae without sclerotic bodies, which are characteristic of chromoblastomycosis. The clinical presentation with nasal and palatal involvement also favors phaeohyphomycosis.

rejected.why: Chromoblastomycosis is typically associated with sclerotic bodies on histopathology and different fungal species on culture; the absence of these features and the specific culture result make it less likely.
